text:
Jason Dickinson came to Edmonton to do the hard minutes, and the Edmonton Journal wrote this week that his defensive game is a microcosm of an improved Oilers team. There's a real case for that. Evolving-Hockey had him taking chances away at the 86th percentile last season against the toughest competition in the league.

Our numbers this season are less kind. At five on five the Oilers get only 29% of the expected goals with him on, and they're far better without him. Part of that is the job: Evolving-Hockey noted he faces top lines and plays with weaker teammates than most.

He has five points in 16 games, two goals on 1.5 expected, which is fine for the role. The Oilers' six-game winning streak ended in Tampa on Nov 19, and they lost again in Carolina two nights later.

What to watch: whether the on-ice numbers move toward the defensive reputation. One of them has to give.
